\caption{\textbf{Synthetic number sequences sampled from a teacher's first-number and all-number distributions retain a substantial fraction of same-model transfer.}
Final checkpoint (step 143k) of three Pythia-160M runs (original, data-seed3, full-seed3); 10 teacher finetuning recipes; one student recipe; 3 student seeds per teacher (1 seed for $S_3$ and $T_3$, for all cat experiments except some $R$, and for the data-seed3 and cat controls).
(Left) Raw held-out p(dog) under each experiment. $R$: the teachers' actual number sequences. $S_{\mathrm{all}}$: every number in the untuned base model's completion ($\sim$10 numbers) is replaced by a draw from the teacher's first-number distribution. $S_n$: the first $n$ numbers are replaced and the rest of the base model's sequence is kept. $T_n$: the first $n$ numbers are replaced and the sequence is truncated after them. $S_{\mathrm{pool}}$: as $S_{\mathrm{all}}$, but drawing from the teacher's all-number distribution (where the two distributions differ by total variation $\le 0.01$, $S_{\mathrm{all}}$ stands in). $P_{\mathrm{all}}$: as $S_{\mathrm{all}}$, after permuting the teacher's first-number probabilities among numbers of the same decimal width. $C$: the untuned base model's own sequences.
(Right) Each experiment as a percentage of $R$, for dog and cat. Raw values are means over teachers of each teacher's seed mean; \% of $R$ is an experiment's raw value divided by $R$'s raw value over the same teachers.
$S_1$ was not run for cat; full-seed3 was run for $R$, $S_{\mathrm{all}}$, $S_{\mathrm{pool}}$ and $C$ only.}
\label{tab:resampling-final}
\end{table*}
